svg.title: BITTER PapRAT kill chain
svg.desc: Single-lane chain of six stages: diplomatic lures to South Asian organizations; an LNK that abuses ftp.exe with an .ico file as a script and creates a Microsoft-update scheduled task; curl tasking with err.log and abc.pdf; VHDX or RAR delivery of an MSI with a Type 194 CustomAction; PapRAT C++ and Rust implants plus WmRAT; and response break points. Critical stages are the ftp.exe bang-escape chain, the MSI drop and the RAT beacon. Detection anchors are Sigma 01-03, KQL k1-k3, YARA, Suricata sids 9970001-9970003 and PEAK H1-H3.
svg.text: BITTER (TA397): PapRAT via ftp.exe .ico scripts and Type 194 MSI droppers
Vendor: FortiGuard Labs (2026-11-02) · Date: 2026-11-09 · Cluster: BITTER (high per FortiGuard) · Day 139
SOUTH ASIA ESPIONAGE LANE
Lures: diplomatic invitations to South Asian government, energy and engineering staff [T1566.001 T1204.002]
Three chains over several months (FortiGuard, 2026-11-02): VHDX 'Letter from the Ambassador - 11th Belt and Road Summit',
RAR 'Official Invitation Majilis 2026 Gala Dinner', 'NV-683 Request for Bilateral Meeting during 22nd HACGAM'
Targets South Asian organizations; telemetry also in Southeast Asia and South Korea
Letter from the Ambassador - 11th Belt and Road Summit.vhdx
Chain 1: LNK launches ftp.exe on an .ico file; ftp bang escape runs it as a script [T1218 T1059.003 T1053.005]
Argument example '!more res.ico': ftp runs the rest as a local shell command, so icon.ico / res.ico hold commands, not images
Script creates a scheduled task posing as a Microsoft (or BIOS) update; shows fake 'Explorer was unable to open this file!'
No PapRAT binary in this chain; operators change the commands server-side
ftp.exe ... res.ico -> cmd -> schtasks + curl
Chain 1 tasking: curl pulls a Base64 script; err.log holds commands, abc.pdf recon [T1105 T1083 T1071.001]
curl contacts C2 and pulls a Base64-encoded script that fetches more commands from a second URL; output kept in err.log
Recon: directory listings, tasks and processes, installed AV, drives, Desktop / Documents / Downloads; uploaded then deleted
OffSeq lists talk.log and ucl.php?svr=%computername%**%username% as URL shapes
techtalkhelp[.]com/talk.log err.log abc.pdf
Chains 2 and 3: VHDX or RAR plus LNK, then an MSI with a Type 194 action [T1204.002 T1218.007 T1036.005]
VHDX shows a LNK; hidden decoy spreadsheet and Visa_Details.msi; LNK runs the MSI in background while the decoy opens
Chain 3: RAR URL shortcut pulls an LNK over WebDAV from rappellingaart[.]com, then Imp_Details.msi drops PapRAT
The MSI has no real install function; Xcitium reads Type 194 as asynchronous executable-from-Binary-table
Visa_Details.msi Imp_Details.msi rappellingaart[.]com
PapRAT (C++ and Rust) and WmRAT: 8 to 11 commands, screenshots, upload, download [T1573.001 T1113 T1140]
C++ bruzsvc.exe (Microsoft version resource): plaintext HTTP beacon every 10 s, C2 data XOR 0x50, ClientID user_computer
Rust build (requpap.pdb, papsolutions): waits 42 s, polls every 5 s over HTTPS, ROT-3 reversed strings; adds MS2 SLP BYE
PapRAT then fetches vnces.exe (WmRAT); commands: msg FDD DEL RUN GDR SS1 UPP DWW
www[.]rivingtonclarks[.]com/beautiQuewonders/banaNa.php
Response and break points [no technique]
Block the eight domains at DNS and proxy; alert on ftp.exe with an .ico argument and on msiexec from a mounted VHDX
Block or warn on VHDX / RAR from mail, disable auto-mount of disk images for standard users, remove Microsoft-update-named tasks
Indicators decay and the primary Fortinet blog was not read: re-validate every domain before blocking
ftp.exe + .ico | VHDX mount | msiexec Type 194
Detection anchors
Sigma 01-03, KQL k1-k3, YARA (2 rules), Suricata sids 9970001-9970003, PEAK H1-H3. Derived from secondary reports of the FortiGuard research.
Break points: DNS and proxy block, ftp.exe with .ico alert, VHDX / RAR mail filtering, task review. Primary Fortinet blog not read; no sample analysis.
